title: Ghost and Contact
premise: Rosalind Marchetti—formerly four other people—has spent seven years buried after exposing a private intelligence firm's black-site operations. When a burner phone rings with the voice of her dead handler, Marcus Vale, she learns he survived and is offering the location of a defector carrying the firm's master ledger—but accepting the call means her old identity resurfaces, and the people hunting her are already closing in. As Rosalind assembles a makeshift crew of other erased witnesses, she discovers the defector extraction is a trap designed to flush out every ghost Vale ever created, and that Vale himself is playing a longer game: buying their escape with his own surrender. In the end, Rosalind chooses to stop running—testifying under her real name, first given to her, and finally letting a found family know who she actually is.
about_author: Casper Delacroix is the pen name of a former logistics coordinator who spent a decade moving people and paperwork across borders they never saw. They write thrillers about the administrative machinery of disappearance, and about the strangers who become the only family the erased can trust.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Rosalind, living as 'Nadia' in a Rotterdam boarding house, rehearses her evacuation routine and refuses a neighbor kid's birthday invitation. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the loneliness of permanent readiness, and the first crack in her armor when she almost says yes.

chapters.title: Number You Should Not Have
chapters.summary: A burner phone appears in her mail slot with no sender. It rings; the voice is Marcus Vale—her handler, officially dead for seven years. He names her real name and a defector: 'the Ledger is on the table.' POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past has her address.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Woman
chapters.summary: Flashback-threaded chapter tracing her four identities and the whistle-blowing that erased them. She burns the boarding-house room and moves. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: grief for every self she's had to kill.

chapters.title: The Man Who Answers to Dead
chapters.summary: Vale directs her to a Hamburg safehouse to meet the extraction team: ex-analyst Priya, forger Tomas, and driver Kofi—each a former witness the firm erased. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: wary recognition; these strangers share her scars.

chapters.title: Ledger, Bait, Ledger
chapters.summary: Priya decodes Vale's message and concludes the defector—firm accountant Elena Sarr—may be bait to flush the ghosts out. Rosalind decides to go anyway. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: the team's first argument and first act of trust.

chapters.title: Vienna, Off the Books
chapters.summary: The crew infiltrates a firm front company to confirm Elena's location, nearly tripping a biometric alarm. Rosalind sees her own file in the archive—her real name redacted by someone inside. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: fury sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Redaction Hand
chapters.summary: Tomas traces the redaction to a firm archivist, Ilsa Brandt, who once protected witnesses—and who may still be alive inside. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: hope as a dangerous habit.

chapters.title: Kofi's Long Drive
chapters.summary: A tense overnight drive to Vienna's outskirts as firm trackers sweep the highways; Kofi tells his story of the family he lost by staying visible. POV: Kofi. Emotional beat: found family solidifying under pressure.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Rosalind makes contact with Elena Sarr through a dead-drop protocol only Vale would know—proof the defector is genuine, or proof the trap is perfect. Elena sends one word: 'Hurry.' POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the pull of rescue against the smell of a trap.

chapters.title: What Vale Buried
chapters.summary: Vale surfaces in person, older and burned, and admits he faked his death to build the extraction—but refuses to say who else knows. Rosalind doesn't fully believe him. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the ache of a mentor who is both anchor and question mark.

chapters.title: The Extraction Plan
chapters.summary: The team maps Elena's guarded safehouse: a 90-second window during a prisoner transfer. Priya insists on a abort condition; Rosalind quietly plans to ignore it. POV: Priya. Emotional beat: loyalty strained by Rosalind's self-destructive courage.

chapters.title: Ninety Seconds
chapters.summary: The extraction: Kofi's drive, Tomas's forged credentials, Rosalind pulling Elena from the transfer convoy as alarms rise. They get her out—but the convoy was expecting them. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: adrenaline, then dread.

chapters.title: The Trap Springs
chapters.summary: Firm hunters hit the safehouse minutes after they leave; the crew scatters. Kofi is captured covering the retreat. POV: Kofi. Emotional beat: sacrifice, and the terror of being known again.

chapters.title: Interrogation Light
chapters.summary: Kofi, held in a black site, stalls his interrogator and feeds false team details—while Rosalind, watching a hijacked camera feed, realizes the firm's director, Anselm Rook, is running the trap personally. POV: Kofi. Emotional beat: defiance as dignity.

chapters.title: Elena's Ledger
chapters.summary: Elena reveals the ledger isn't documents—it's her memory of every witness the firm erased, including where Rook buried the bodies of the ones who talked. She is the archive. POV: Elena. Emotional beat: the weight of being evidence.

chapters.title: Brandt's Price
chapters.summary: Ilsa Brandt, alive and cornered, offers the black site's layout in exchange for extraction—her redactions were protection, she claims. Tomas vouches; Priya objects. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a gamble.

chapters.title: The Exchange Vale Wanted
chapters.summary: Vale confesses the full plan: he intends to trade himself to Rook for Kofi and a corridor out, ending the hunt by becoming the story. Rosalind refuses to let him. POV: Vale. Emotional beat: a handler finally telling the truth, too late to matter.

chapters.title: Storming the Quiet House
chapters.summary: The team raids the black site using Brandt's layout: Priya cuts power, Tomas forges a transfer order, Rosalind and Vale go in for Kofi. It works—until Rook springs his second trap. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the climax's ignition; everything on the line at once.

chapters.title: Rook's Offer
chapters.summary: Cornered, Rook offers Rosalind her old life back—full restoration, records wiped—if she hands over Elena and the ledger. She answers by broadcasting the ledger's first page to every screen in the building. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: the refusal that defines her.

chapters.title: Vale's Corridor
chapters.summary: Vale surrenders himself to Rook to buy the others' escape, dying—or disappearing—in the exchange as the site burns. Rosalind carries Elena out through the smoke. POV: Vale. Emotional beat: grief and inheritance; the mentor's last lesson is sacrifice.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Weeks later, in a Hague hearing room, Rosalind testifies under her real name—Rosalind Marchetti, first given—with Priya, Tomas, Kofi, and Elena in the gallery. Rook's network cracks. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into voice.

chapters.title: The Unpacked Bag
chapters.summary: Rosalind unpacks the go-bag for the first time in seven years, hangs a coat in a shared closet, and answers the door when the neighbor kid knocks. The burner phone rings one last time; she lets it. POV: Rosalind. Emotional beat: stillness earned; the ghost becomes a person again.
